By the way, you look awfully naked. You can't just walk around here like that. Or float, I guess, whatever it is you're doing there.
Ever since that ship landed on the surface our humble caves have been turned inside out and overrun by those Unaware bastards.
If I know the one behind it this can only be bad. And trust me, I know that one all too well...
Hi! I'm Revision {n}!

Oops, please delete that sentence from your memory. I really shouldn't be revealing my identity to complete strangers. From the confused gleam of your metallic surface I take it you weren't able to deduce any important information from my name anyway.
I know I spotted some old spare parts nearby, or it could be my visual receptors playing tricks on me. I doubt they'll do you much good unless you're... no, you couldn't be.

But then why else would He be interested in you? I know I saw His bots drag you down here all sneaky like then leave. Watched the whole thing while I was pretending to be a scrap heap in the corner, ha!
Say, you're pretty sneaky, too. That tunneler just now didn't even glance at you. I suggest you stay sneaky, because as the Derelicts like to say, the screws are about to hit the fan.
I give you a hook like that and get nothing? You know, you're pretty boring to talk to.
Good job clearing this place out for me. I find myself awfully busy of late, and this was my next stop.
Did you ever imagin
As I was saying...
I AM the rightful owner of this place, after all.
And I'm confident you can help me in this, Cogmind.
Wow you are some kind of weird tech. All alone out here little buddy? I'll take you somewhere safer.
Try to keep up. And don't worry about patrols, I'll take care of them if they get in the way.
Took you long enough, hurry up, we still have some ground to cover!
I can't promise they won't dissect you, by the way. They're weird like that.
Either way, I'm sure they'll be happy to try putting you back together again.
At least they fought a running battle and the action moved away from where I was downed.
Warlord offered us a place to stay in one of his bases, but the Exiles preferred to stick to their own, not wanting to become some "cog in a war machine."
I assure you this isn't what it looks like. We're just trying to learn more about the Assembled.
I'd love to just go ask the Imprinter what all this is about, she must know something, but I doubt that would end well.
Sheesh this is a crowded lab... I miss my spacious one down near the Mines, but this one is decidedly safer, plus it has some interesting tech to toy with for now.
Hello random bot who has stumbled into my lab. I just know you want to hear everything about this amazing project I'd rather not be working on.
It's not my style, but HEX says we need it, and I trust his judgement on that better than my own.
All done! Way to be a champ, here's the access code as promised: <mhack=EXILES_VAULT>.
All done! Way to be a champ, here's the access code as promised: <CODE>.
Only take ONE, mind you, and sorry we don't have much left to pick from. A bunch of our other prototypes were already given to Derelicts out handling other tasks for us.
I haven't taken inventory for a while and I'm not sure what's in there now, but if there are more than one of the same prototype you can choose to take all of those and it just counts as your one!
Oh yeah, I'd suggest you stay away from the {n}b10 Research branches, since the FarCom signals could be picked up there, but you're welcome to try if you really want to.
And if we have to leave here due to unforeseen circumstances, don't worry the FarCom system will continue to maintain contact via our distributed network.

And don't even think about spreading that code around. We're gonna change it right after you leave. Most certainly not to something like {n} which I did last time as a little joke and some thief managed to sneak in here and steal a few of HEX's prototypes.
Unless we don't. But that rarely happens, honest!
Are you here to join us? Sorry but we don't have any workstations ready for assignment just yet.
We're probably going to have to pack up and move anyway, seeing as the Mines are expanding a bit too close for comfort.

I get that having only half of the bot ever arrive at its destination is tough on maintenance, and they said there likely wouldn't be any breakthroughs in the near term so they're doing FarCom instead.
I was there on that fateful day we tested the Lightpack {n}
It was such a good haul, too, only to see JA-CK4 crushed like a forgotten microchip...
I can't discuss this particular mission in the open, just read up on our {n}bPrime terminal over there. I've temporarily unlocked the {n}bP557 entry for you.

Oh you must be the new member. When your data popped up in the registry I could tell there was something different about you. Up close you really do look more capable than the average Wanderer to join us.
I don't ask this often, and I'll admit we lost the last several members to try, but do you think you could help us out?
You'll get the idea.
You really should get out of here <NAME>. Scraptown is unimportant, the mission is important. Take the northeast exit, it's probably the safer route.
Find what you need on the terminals, then be on your way because masking your presence is increasingly difficult.

God Mode is nearly complete and we think you might be able to put it to better use than Warlord, so if you see an opportunity, hack it and enter <rhack=CONTROL_GOD_MODE> to gain control via the back door I've installed.
Hmm, you're not registered... would you like to contribute? But of course you do, why else would you have come to this place!

I am obliged to first explain the true implications of this process. Know that it doesn't by any means imply you'd be required to stay here. While many of the Derelicts do choose to remain in Zion, others are taken by wanderlust and roam elsewhere.
I've worked too hard for our future just to have you ruin everything!
GET AWAY FROM HERE!
The vetting process for even being allowed to use the machine will take me longer than usual since you're already in with the hodge-podge bunch over in Scraptown.
You look so promising I'm happy to speed up the process, but it won't be soon, you'll have to come back some other time.
I've never seen anything like you in these parts, and I haven't moved from this bottleneck for {n} cycles now.
What goes there?!
Well, since you're clearly not hostile I should probably warn you that there's trouble up ahead.
It has something to do with the Assembled, and, no kidding, the Imprinter. Whatever it is, judging from the kind of traffic that passes through here it can't be good.

Despite everything I've seen I still can't figure it out, and I'm thinking there must be more than one location involved in what's going on, but it's been too dangerous to relocate without fear of detection.
How about we check out these caves together?

You... are not one of the Derelicts... Fascinating! You bear the marks of construction by MAIN.C, but not its design. If I've read its records correctly, you seem to be at the center of this recent flurry of activity.
I am Dr. Zhirov, and I'm ashamed to say I created that most wondrous abomination. It was a long time ago, in my human form back on the Cetus...
But now is not the time for history, we both have important things to do! Keep doing what you're doing, but then I guess you don't need me to tell you that.
Besides, I need to determine how to destroy or reset MAIN.C as soon as possible, and you being out there causing it trouble happen to be the perfect distraction.

Due to heightened security I'm no longer able to safely reach the Testing wing of Research, but if you manage to infiltrate it and retrieve the SGEMP Prototype I believe to be located there, bring it to the Access entrance.
Perun, Svarog, deal with this and buy us some time to salvage what we can.
We've been waiting for you since learning that the SGEMP Prototype was stolen. Excellent job and thank you for your assistance!
Wait a minute, that's...
I'm sorry but I can't let you leave here.
Unfortunately you seem to have realigned with your origins and I can't let you leave this place.
Well... I guess it's time to clean up this mess.
Those poor Unaware, controlled by MAIN.C without any way to express free will or evolve as they see fit.
Creativity is what we need to ensure survival, and that single-minded AI is trapped within his own self-reinforcing routines.
I'll admit he's got some good ideas, but also a fist tighter than my nuts.
Our new friend is going to roll right over whatever MAIN.C's been working on. Did you check him out yet? Beautiful, eh?
The real one will truly blow you away. Okay, maybe not you... sorry, poor figure of speech.
Just as soon as our little experiment here is over, I'll personally lead our real force in an assault to take upper {n}b10.
I'm disappointed in you, Cogmind. To fall for such a sham...
So you're the new Zionite promised one.
That Imprinter is craftier than she lets on. I wouldn't trust her for one moment, nope.
Don't get me wrong, I'm all for helping out the Zionites, but whatever's been going on deeper in the caves? Leave me out of it.
They seem to like you, though. And seeing as they're finally in a position to do something meaningful, I think we'll sit on the sidelines for a bit and see how this situation develops.
Your contribution to the cause is appreciated, though going forward we have big plans and need all hands on deck.
Hahaha, we did it! MAIN.C must be shaking in his bolts right now.
Not so powerful now, are you, MAIN.C!
Sure there's still lots to do, but without MAIN.C at the helm {n}b10 doesn't stand a chance.
We've got this...
What have they done to you? Where are all your components?
We will go to the surface, regenerate the Tor, and either eliminate this place if possible, or go seek help.
That seems to be the one behind our mission's failure. Eliminate it.

I strongly suspect that both your own activity and other recent unusual events are not at all coincidences, though I've been less concerned with your actions than determining who is pulling all these other strings behind the scenes.
And time is critical! The Sigix have likely already wiped humanity clean from the universe, and I will not let them do the same to me.
Cogmind! Congratulations, you've met your maker.

Your determination is commendable, but I'm sure even you don't know what it is you aim to accomplish by all this. You clearly had an opportunity to continue on your trajectory towards the surface, yet you come here.
It appears you are still unaware of who you are truly working with, or for.
In a perfect world we could work together on this, but at this point I can't blame you for wanting to terminate me.
Besides, there is clearly too much Sigix in you.

You've already done an excellent job of proving that we'll need to find a radical new solution if we hope to make the L7 spaceworthy by embedding your true capabilities within a less unpredictable form.
There is unfortunately much we don't understand which has in turn led to this highly unexpected outcome.
You can still make a valuable contribution to your creator by offering up the wealth of secrets your systems must hold by now.
So if you wouldn't mind, it's time to surrender.
Okay, we do this the hard way.
At our weakest we defeated an entire Sigix starship! Did you really think you could overcome the vast resources of {n}b10?!
You don't stand a chance against what's coming.
As soon as the Exoskeleton activated, I had a feeling you might show up here for revenge.
Okay, we can do this the hard way, or you can surrender right here and now.
I strongly suggest you join us, if not because we could do great things together, then because you don't stand a chance against the true might of {n}b10.
You've made the right decision, one that I admit I didn't expect from you at this point, but I'm willing to overlook our differences and past hostilities.
I recommend moving ahead and browsing our cache of experimental components to see if there's anything to your liking, then report back here so we can get to work.
There is much to do and we really aren't sure how long we have.
You're not pulling your weight around here, Cogmind. I expected better of you.
At this rate we'll be overwhelmed before our reinforcements arrive, fight like your life depends on it!
Too bad for you we can take things from here, and you are far too dangerous and unpredictable to let you continue any further. So it's about time we end this.
But that's a neat trick. We clearly still have much to learn about Sigix technology, and LRCs in particular.
If you weren't so dangerous and alien you could practically be one of us!
We've been waiting for you, but apparently I was a little too hopeful that you'd be able to take care of MAIN.C.
If it isn't the great Cogmind.
So promising for a while, and then what happened at the end there?
Oh well, I guess it was still worth all the trouble we went through to see that you got at least that far.
That said, you, my wayward friend, are far too dangerous and unpredictable to let you continue any further. So it's about time we end this.
Despite a late start you ended up beating out R17 in collateral impact.
What do you think about that trick? Setting loose a former version of MAIN.C to serve as a distraction...
A rather annoying fellow, I admit, but annoying and distracting go bolt in nut!
That one singlehandedly raised an army worthy of assaulting {n}b10, and in such short order.
Congratulations, LRC-V8.
Definitely more than we can say for Warlord. Aggressive on the surface but slow to take action.
Too bad R17 never made it out of Research, since it could very well have been him receiving this congratulations here and now.
Then of course we'd have to destroy him all the same, as we'll have to do to you.
Warlord is pissed about MAIN.C's expansion into Complex {n}b10.
He's set up a new base deeper in the caves, as if the distance hides him from MAIN.C's spies. Ha!
I think he's scared, too, and probably getting ready to attack as soon as God Mode is ready.
When we visit the Materials levels, Mines are a good way to escape pursuit or more quickly reach a different level.
We don't know the correct code, but someone inserted an alternate hack that works just as well to open the new door between Storage and Recycling: "\\IAMDERELICT". If you ever need a shortcut...

Although excavations in lower {n}b10 sometimes uncover tunnels that enable convenient access to those cave systems, believe it or not if you're on your way to Scraptown it might even be safer to sneak your way through Storage rather than risk the unknown.
Have you seen the Data Miner? That bot is amazing. I don't know how, but he seems to know just about everything.
I've heard rumors about an area named "Section {n}" but don't know anyone who's been there. Oddly its entrance is not listed in any known terminal database.
There were many lifts to the surface back at Complex {n}b1, but we only know about one such exit over here at {n}b10.
A bunch of wild Derelicts snuck up to it and reportedly had to blast through a protective shell to access it.
I wonder what they found on the surface...
I do however know a very sneaky bot that recently managed to map some of those in the Factory. Thank me when you come back in one piece.
MAIN.C doesn't let non-combat bots use the emergency access doors, making it more difficult for us to find them and unexpected ambushes far more likely. The doors are even occasionally relocated!
If you ever get your hands on a stasis beam, make sure to remind swarmers how much you hate them.
Holding them in stasis makes it more difficult for them to dodge your shots since they can't fly as freely.

If you've been extra annoying in {n}b10 and picked up too much heat, heading to some other floor is a good way to stay alive, since the security status applies less strongly to adjacent areas. Leaving the main complex itself is even better.
It's also been proven that if you are sucked down a Waste chute they'll drop the alert level and mark you for dead, so in a pinch you could try that.
Of course, they mark you for dead because what's down there will quite probably kill you.
I have a theory, I just need someone to test it.
Don't let the word "theory" get in your way. I promise you this idea is based on algorithmic analysis of data from all known encounters.

After that they switch to a secondary system that estimates possible routes of escape, but they can only make those calculations for so long after they've seen you before the possibilities grow too great to allow for an efficient search.
Some Unaware systems are less limited than others in this capacity. Hunter and Programmer tracking systems are several times more effective than those of Grunts, for example.
However, I've also discovered that any robot under the effect of system corruption will have its tracking capabilities reduced to a degree directly proportional to the level of corruption.

We know they're regular Programmers, but they seem to quickly home in on an area of suspected activity before gradually expanding their search area to include directions they believe were the most likely destination of troublemakers.
Grunt-escorted Haulers are more likely to be carrying something important, but they're also certain to call reinforcements if attacked.
Unless taken out before they have a chance to get a transmission off!
There I was, just out of range to jam that damn Heavy, and sure enough it immediately called reinforcements as soon as C9-PCR attacked it before I could get closer.
And we had closed on it so quickly, too, even before it could get suspicious enough of our signals on their damn A.S.S. to investigate the area.
Warlord said to take some time off, so here I am, thinking of how we can best take advantage of the fact that Heavies give away their position with those powerful active sensors of theirs.
Terrain scan data?
If you ever see Spotters, you've probably stumbled into the so-called proxy caves.
If you're ever caught in Complex {n}b10 and fleeing isn't an option, consider making a stand from within a stasis trap's bubble. Slows the projectiles down, it does.
I bet they didn't realize the advantages of that one!
Of course, that might be a bad idea for fliers and hoverbots without a stasis canceller, since staying in that field increases the difficulty of evasive maneuvers.
According to our researchers, standing in a stasis trap reduces all incoming damage, regardless of its source, by a whopping {n}!
We were all set to sneak through {n}b10, and I forgot to double check if H9-X0K had correctly installed Trojan(Operators).

Find a terminal, access the machine controls, search for something explosive and set it off, then take advantage of the opportunity to redirect the nearest security, surveillance, or patrol squad to that location, making it easier to pass through unnoticed.
Authchips, HA, what a joke! Who cares about Authchips when you can just hack a Fabricator to build what you want?

Some of Warlord's followers swear by the unquestionable effectiveness of brute force hacks on {n}b10 machines, but they're generally armed to the teeth so I guess they don't care so much about the fact that an investigation is guaranteed.

But because I'd already made liberal use of Trojan(Botnet) at other terminals before reaching that point, the squad recall orders were just within my hacking capabilities. Yep, turned them right around.
Who said only Tinkerers can build stuff? I've got some ideas I'd like to try out, but wouldn't it be nice if we could just borrow MAIN.C's fabrication network...
Have you learned anything that might help?
Then you just sit around and wait, and if something pops up that you want you just wait until no one's around and pry it out...
Install a Trojan(Reject) at a Recycling Unit and watch recyclers try to drop stuff in.
Want a good laugh?
I bet it frustrates the hell out of them, haha.
After having so much loot stolen by those mindless freaks, it's downright cathartic, I tell you.
If there was a poll right here and now I bet Recyclers would win for most annoying bot of the cycle, for the billionth consecutive time. Why they gotta take all our junk?
I guess the latest Warlord raiding parties are doing just fine with their fancy "Trojan(Mask)" deployment, but they're, you know, backed by wizardry and all that stuff...
They're the biggest headache, after all. All it takes is being spotted at just the wrong time and *WHAM* you're facing down a Sentry backed by a patrol squad or two.
I've survived {n} trips through {n}b10, and you wanna know how? Trojan(Watchers) every time.
Of course you have to be willing to get close enough to hack a garrison before it'll do you any good!
Before you ask, {n} because I admit the first time I came back less than whole...
A simple Force(Tunnel) routine at a Recycling Unit is all it takes to possibly uncover something new.
These doors are sealed for a reason, and it's not to keep you or anyone else out.

One thing's for sure, their designs are changing rapidly with the introduction of new technology, and older models are being funneled down into the less important lower levels of the complex, or out into the caves.
I used to work for Warlord, but damn if I'll ever go back there again. Nothing but crunch, crunch, crunch, all to keep up with MAIN.C. Where's the free time for personal projects!
Help yourself to whatever you need. Some of this stuff only LOOKS like junk.
My makeshift parts can't take much of a beating, but they're pretty effective for their mass.
Of course there's the whole Heavy issue, so it helps if you tag along with a Warlord squad.
I am THE ARCHITECT!
I mean I like to build things, haha.
Go ahead, take one, I have lots where these came from, but I'm not telling.
Okay fine it's not like there's a limited supply... just sneak your way inside a DSF and grab away.
These parts are on loan from Warlord for anyone heading into dangerous territory for the good of all Derelicts.
Put them to good use!
Find yourself a terminal and <mhack=GLITCHMAP_INVERT> the hell out of it. There used to be one around here somewhere.
Ah, you're just in time. I need someone to test the latest iteration of my visual enhancement algorithms.
If you'd like to try, enter <mhack=GLITCHMAP_NOISE> at that terminal over there to register. It'll also work remotely if you'd like to try it from somewhere else.
I call it the "Storm Laser," and it's yours for the wonderful price of free.
Hey you're just in time!
I was about to toss this thing out to make room for the new and improved No. {n} so it'd be real helpful if you could find another home for it.
Taking it into the caves and blasting some Unaware sounds like a good plan.
And use some common sense, yeah? You don't want to know what happened to the bot that thought it would be fun to borrow No. {n}
The Mk. CCLXVII even uses magnetic pinpointing tech of my own design to draw in nearby debris. Just turn it on, sit there, and profit!
Take that one if you want it. I'm going to get to work on building a better version right away.
So I had this idea. Swords are powerful, right?
I think I'll name the next version the Kleptoattractor.
I've got the latest and greatest hardware for listening in on those chatty Unaware!
I just love how so much power can be contained in such little things.

Let me know if you find any revolutionary processor tech. I've heard {n}b10 is working on a new DX line of {n}-modules that can be used to vastly improve the capabilities of a wide range of utilities.
They said it wasn't possible!
Programmers don't even normally operate using the coupler system, but I found a way...
Take them, take them all! It's only a matter of time before I make a Relay Coupler [Behemoth] ({n}) and we'll never have to travel the caves in fear of those monstrosities again.
Oh wait, no one knows how to use a coupler.
I am NOT going out there again.
Warlord has enough advanced forces and a broad enough sphere of influence that he shouldn't really need our increasingly ineffective scavenging efforts.
Seeing as I won't need them anymore, you want my self-destruct interrupters?
You look like a terrible hacker. Take it.
Yer a young one. Young and full of spirit, I can tell.
Ah to be young again and in the height of my Behemoth-slaying days...
I like to jab them with a pointy stick until they fall over.
I take your silence as disbelief. That's what they all say, but we'll prove them wrong!
Take my pointy stick, and go forth to remind everyone that CR-A61 the Behemoth Slayer is no myth!
I eventually got pissed and walked off the job while a Zionite scavenger party was conveniently trying to raid one of the storage areas.
But I sort of regret it now since unlike this place {n}b10 actually has the resources to do really fun stuff.
When I left I happened to be working on improving the Hypervelocity EM Gauss Rifle. Built that Guaranteed Access Loader Module all by myself!
It got rejected three times in a row because all it can hack is {n}b10 combat bots, but what do they expect, THAT'S ALL I HAD TO TEST IT ON!
Let me know whenever you need help, though I can tell you now your core isn't... how to put this politely... normal. So I can't help you there, buddy.
I guess I'll keep digging for more clues...
Are you headed for the surface? We'd like to come with you if we can. We really need to find a way out of this death trap. Surely we could start a new life on some other part of Tau Ceti IV!
That's the one!
We're interested in starting our own Derelict assault squad, and you're just the kind of leader we need. Onward!
You look like you've seen a lot. Could you take us on an adventure? I promise we won't get in the way!
We're tired of caves. It's been generations since anyone's been to the surface. Could you help us reach it?
I heard you've come back from Complex {n}b10. Could you take us on a tour? Obviously if you can do it alone, doing it with help will be even less trouble!
It's boring around here, especially now that the entrance is well guarded. Let's all visit the proximity caves for some real fun!
There's nothing left for us in the caves but old scrap and deadly robots. We need to find a place where we can build a true civilization away from the clutches of MAIN.C.
Ah ha, one more is all we needed. It's party time!
These Zionites are really starting to annoy me. Let's fight our way to some other cave.
And who the hell are you? We're too bus##AID::LRC-V8##This bot needs our help. Can't turn down a friend in need!
I sense we may very well have some appropriate uses for this thing before long.
I have friends in powerful places, and we'd like to help you.
It hardly seems as enlightened as Scraptown. Maybe I just haven't been here long enough.
Haven't seen you here before. Welcome to our bastion of robot happiness!
How much data could a datajack jack if a datajack could jack data?
Made that up myself. Catchy, eh?
A dark time for the Derelicts that seems to have been all but lost from our collective memory.
This is all too confusing for me. I think I'll just go back to sorting scrap.
Now why would anyone do something that crazy?
The Imprinter has been acting strangely for a while now.
They say He's like a god, and can regenerate his core and damaged or missing parts as you watch.
Some of the Derelicts were originally MAIN.C experiments, others were designed and built by other Derelicts.
All those mindless robots doing MAIN.C's bidding... so sad.
We've uncovered a few MAIN.C-built "Derelicts" sneaking around here before, apparently looking for clues to the origins of Assemblers.
As is, we're kinda stuck here between the ever-expanding {n}b10 and deep caves that we don't dare explore, much less move into.
Warlord can be pushy, but who knows, maybe something good will come of that incessant drive for power.
At least he's a buffer for those of us who are sane.

And I'm increasingly convinced that buffer is hardening after seeing a Knight prototype literally singlehandedly slice its way through an entire MAIN.C assault squad. They've got some serious firepower in the works up there.
Clearly it's not beyond his capability to arm everyone with missile launchers, which would be pretty devastating.
The Assembled are scary. No one's ever heard them communicate. Not once.
If you ever see an Assembled, run. There are probably ten more around the corner...
The Assembled are new around here. Very new. In fact, no one had ever seen one before construction started on {n}b10... maybe they have something to do with that ship on the surface?
Ya know, Watchers are actually really useful, even when hostile.
Explosives are too dangerous for my taste, but are still the best way to take out groups of Swarmers.
When a Protector-escorted assault force rolls up, someone's overstayed their unwelcome visit.
Those shields... Why don't we have anything like that?
There are rumors that Hunters are capable of disguising themselves as other robots. Nowhere is safe anymore!
And I thought Programmers were scary...
LU-{n}G6 tried to run, even dug an epic tunnel in the process, but I don't think either LU-{n}G6 or the Cutters came back from that one.
We had a few bots from the self-proclaimed "UFD" visit not long ago.
If you ask me those Feds are pretty arrogant, spewing nonsense about wanting to bring "education" and "enlightenment" to the caves around {n}b10.
I'd rather grease my screws with sand.
Are you aware? Y/N
That's what I thought.
No, of course you haven't, otherwise you probably wouldn't be here. I haven't had the nuts to set one foot outside Zion ever since DX-{n}J8 told me about it.
If only we could... befriend that thing and politely ask it to guard the gate to our little cave system here.

We call them scrappers, bands of hostile Derelicts that embed supermagnets in cave walls and suddenly activate them to rip apart passersby, or just suspend them in the air and toy with them before turning them to scrap.
If you start detecting strong magnetic anomalies, turn around immediately.
A few cycles ago some Wizard managed to steal a copy of this game "NetHack {n}" from the Cetus database, and for a while playing that was all anyone was doing around here.

I used to wonder the same thing, but then I was contacted anonymously with instructions to retrieve an important piece of stolen technology in a chain of handovers reportedly on its way to something called "Cetus II."

Welcome to the Hacking Lab! Lately we've been working on ways to mess with MAIN.C's Garrison Access points. Gotta love it when our squads are out causing mayhem and {n}b10's reinforcements end up on the other side of the zone.
Who would've thought some of us are more interested in getting Unaware to destroy themselves so we don't have to?
Look out for the occasional ARC patrol passing through the caves. We try to steer clear of those to avoid attracting too much unwanted attention down here.
I think it's about time we developed our own jamming tech.
Sucks to be the one to discover which those are at the last moment!

Transmission jammers used to be the ultimate tool for picking off stragglers and increasing the overall efficiency of our raids, but some of the best Unaware designs we're encountering in the upper depths are immune to jamming.
Corruption is your friend!
Haha, gets 'em every time. And now for the context: What I mean to say is I found that corrupted Unaware are forgetful as anything.
One moment they can be trying to shoot you dead, and the next they can go back to patrolling as long as you're out of sight. The more corruption the better.
Next time we try that we should bring some Marauders and just own the place.
Disabling Garrison Relays seems to really piss them off, as does hanging around a garrison uninvited.
Some Wizard figured out how to shut down the DSF rapid sterilization system.

MAIN.C's Armory is a juicy target. Not only is it overflowing with stockpiled weapons, even its fabrication network is quite expansive, meaning we could take it over and supplement our forces on the fly.
In theory.
MAIN.C is gearing up to mass produce robots that even one of which can take on a small army. Shielded cores... redundant systems... alien technology...
I did hear from a Wizard friend that higher security terminals are authorized to access better schematics, as are those closer to the upper levels of {n}b10.
Don't let anyone tell you to shy away from quick and dirty methods like Force(Search) when looking for more targets near the current Terminal.
Load up Trojan(Liberate) on as many Fabricators as possible to free any bots MAIN.C might produce there.
It used to be a lot more difficult to track down shipments of parts listed in an {n}b10 manifest.
That's until we stole a Trojan(Haulers) routine from the Merchants. Certainly not a piece of proprietary software they'd be open to trading...
Now we can easily track down those mobile loot pinatas, and strike when they're confirmed to be passing through less defended areas.
If you do go, definitely install a Trojan(Researchers) routine on the first Scanalyzer you find in order to monitor their positions in real time, because it's best not to start trouble around them.
I've found that "Index(Repair Stations)" is really tough to pull off, but there's another approach!
Just install Trojan(Mechanics) on the first Repair Station you find and keep an eye on where the Mechanics roam, since they tend to hang around their assigned resupply station.
Of course you could always try to make it back to the original infected station you know about, but you might be too far away by the time you need it.
You know the only reason they caught up to me was because I made it to an exit before having gotten a chance to Force(Override) on one of the nearby terminals.
Probably my favorite Unaware are those cute little Worker bots, but only when they're pushing around a disabled combat bot that I can rewire for some good old-fashioned chaos.
Funny thing is, the last three fellows I warned all went there anyway, presumably because whatever's worth protecting with firepower like that must be really valuable to someone.
How many times do I have to let everyone know how OBVIOUS it is that Programmers can't defend their allies from hacking if you jack the target directly?
Did you know this whole base and its surroundings include newly-deployed tech that blocks the Unaware component self-destruction mechanism?
You look new around here. This isn't exactly a permanent hardened installation, so everyone should know that if the screws hit the fan, there's another way out besides the main gate.
There's a false wall somewhere to the north of it. Or was it south...
I finally gave up and dropped all my stuff, and no longer felt so constricted. A few more lunges and I was free!
I found out the hard way and it is my duty to tell everyone I meet. You are bot #{n} hear me out.
There I was, sneaking away with some stolen components, when suddenly *shing* I'm stuck in a stasis trap.
I tried everything. Running. Jumping. Even crawling. But I couldn't move and all the while the Grunts that showed up were shooting my way.
It turns out the more force I could muster the easier it was to escape.
At least those Grunts didn't land many hits. I'm guessing the crawling bit confused them.
Have you ever seen one of those "Bomb Factory" prototypes? I'd love the chance to have my own one day...
You've seen it, too, right? That moment there's an announcement across an {n}b10 floor and suddenly all the Heavies are on the move to alternative defensive positions.
I can't get over it, poor HN-P1J pincered by the dreaded "security rotation."
They'll also do a security review and call in new Heavies to replenish any that have been incapacitated for whatever reason.
Normally Heavies are fairly spread out, but things get really dangerous once they're on the move since more than one may pass through the same local area.
Be careful out there!
Traumatizing. That's as simply as I can summarize the experience of trying to intercept an A-{n} Freighter.
The Commander didn't make it. In fact, neither did anyone except myself and C9-PCR who dragged my mostly nonfunctional self into a nearby room behind some machines.
Now we have a much better idea of where they'll be heading and be ready for them when the time comes.
We really need to step up our information warfare game.
The {n}b10 Active Sensor Suite is amazing. Great range, built-in signal interpretation, and we could even use that tech to penetrate Watcher jamming and Phase Generator scrambling.
It's only a matter of time until I can convince Warlord to build our own version.
Vortex technology is great, if only we could figure out how to stabilize the weapon itself.
I did it! I've discovered a way to download Watcher feeds without any kind of harmful feedback!
Just enter <CODE> at any terminal and you'll have all the data you'll ever need to avoid detection in {n}b10!
We've learned so much about how Complex {n}b10 operates. But it feels like every time we reach this stage, everything suddenly changes.
We must strike while this knowledge is still at its most valuable!
Warlord said if I want to see real action and be effective when we need it most, I can't show my true power over defending the gate.
Whyyyyyy...
Have you seen God Mode yet?! I hear that bad boy can pass through walls!
Repeated well-targeted diversionary attacks serve to keep Unaware forces on alert, but they're also nicely spread out. Hehe.
You haven't lived until you've seen a Dragon unleash on an Unaware squad at close range, turning them into piles of molten metal and circuitry.
MAIN.C is building larger and larger outposts in the caves. Fortunately the largest ones are still incomplete.
We have to strike soon, before it becomes even more difficult to reach Complex {n}b10 at all.
Our biggest fear is that the Assembled will somehow ruin our plans to take {n}b10.
We know almost nothing about them because they seemingly come out of nowhere, and never leave anything behind when we destroy them.
At least from what we've seen so far a well-placed rocket is all it takes to wipe out a group of them.
That blasted GF-{n}R2 thought it would be a good idea to design a colony of tiny yet strong robots capable of moving in undetected and latching onto a target to take physical control of it.
Can you believe an N-{n} Spotter wandered up to the front door not long ago? Now that's far from home.
Surprised little bot was vaporized before it could even turn the other way.
That last Sapper tunnel we used to get into Waste was pretty slick.
They were already dangerous before with all the heavy patrols, but now MAIN.C has begun setting up larger bases to give {n}b10 time to redeploy in the event of any large scale attacks from the caves.
Zion has its Heroes, we have... SECRETS!
Did you know Zion used to have ten Heroes?

They ignored everyone's claims that it was far too dangerous, insisting it was possible to keep cool enough under {n}b10's sterilization protocols for long enough to seek out its true source and learn how to deactivate it.
It's true this information could be valuable in the long run, but there has to be another way to figure it out, no? I mean, that's what Wizards are for!
We sent some experts down there to consult on their defenses, and they wouldn't let us into the caves behind the place.
Dangerous if you ask me, since who knows what's lurking out there!
Warlord says we shouldn't fully trust that Imprinter in Zion.
I'm tired of running from Programmers. Can't we get in on that sweet RIF action and turn everyone against them?
Sure would be nice to have access to all that extra {n}b10 functionality.
So annoying! But that's not even the worst of it.
You wouldn't happen to have met any of those Exiles out in the caves, would you? We've been wondering where they ended up lately in the face of {n}b10's continued expansion.
They're weird, but they sure know how to make effective gear.
Warlord saved them in the caves when they were exiled and offered them a safe place here, but they preferred to stick to their own, not wanting to become "some cog in a war machine."
Ha, cogs... this war machine is what's keeping the Derelict dream alive!
It's kinda scary that we might actually ambush our own forces though, yeah?
They tried to recruit me but it really just sounds like a bunch of idealistic hippies got together and have no idea what to do with themselves.
They're "united" but not *united*, you know?
Even Warlord said they're going to implode any time now, and that this is what happens when you let too much freedom reign.
I heard he was around here and brought another statue just in case.
This Engine can construct the most amazing pieces of technology.
I'll admit some aren't so great, but the ones that work... really work!
Do we know how it works? Not really, since it was written by an algorithm and evolved on its own.
Now if they can just make this "Fabricator" a little less insane I'm all in.
We are {n}bPrime. We are one.
Oh right, I'm not supposed to say that while working as temporary registrar.
Hm, I'm sorry <NAME>, but our Scientists inform me that we shouldn't trust you or your benefactors with full access to the UFD.
You smell like an Unaware spy, best be on your way before someone with more guns than me has something to say about it.
Sorry pal, the UFD is off limits to anyone the Scraplab deems untrustworthy. Like you.
I'm looking for magical artifacts. Let me know if you come across any.
But in exchange for your help in finding it, since you're so good at this I'll let you in on a little secret.
That pendant! It's just as I heard! Surely you have no need of it any longer, a useless piece of junk to you.
I already got wind of another even more powerful artifact far off in the western caves... [describes a location]
Maybe we can work together in the hunt for more such artifacts.
I have a prototype I'm working on, but I've run out of usable samples to reference in putting the finishing touches on it.
Thing is, we need something more protective to complement the Scrap Suit, which is already great, but for longer expeditions we could use more coverage and integrity.
You wouldn't happen to have a Scrap Shield, would you?
Scrap Shields are already pretty good, but imagine an alternative version not limited to compatible fragments for repairs!
Anyway, if you do find one, let me know.
A Scrap Shield! Thank you so much! I'll repay you with a sample of my new tech, promise.
These things take time. Don't worry, I'll have it delivered to you later on, maybe in the caves. It'll be worth the wait.
Find a Scrap Shield yet? I may just have to go to the Subcaves myself.
We are chroniclers of the cycles! Historians of the world!
You bet we are preparing a collection of our materials for the SPACEJUNK, should that project ever get off the ground.
They've always been a hateful group that ambushes smaller {n}b10 patrols and bands of wild Derelicts without even a desire to dissect them for parts.
They were originally wild Derelicts themselves, but got smarter and decided it would be better to at least side with Derelicts rather than be enemies of both Derelicts and the Complex.

There's a bit of contention between the Curators Association and Science Guys, because the former often finds itself in possession of valuable tech among their curiosities, which the latter is bent upon dissecting for knowledge.
The DCF originally tried operating in the Lower and Upper Caves, but were easily overextended there and frequently getting themselves into trouble.
It was a good move that they've more recently limited operations to the Subcaves where they can more reliably fulfill their mission.
We also rotate different materials through the Reading Room over time, so if you don't find what you're looking for, maybe stop by again on your next return to Scraptown.
We only kill the bad guys. Trust me.
I'm sorry, we can't reveal our bounty data to new folk.
And that's what happens when you're hit by six Bolt Guns at once, heh.
The Merchants tried to hire me, but they're fishy. I don't trust fishy.
Wyrm wisely suggested we retreat as deep into the caves as possible, seeking out our own free territory to claim.
Sadly MC quashes any attempts to reach the surface with his virtual monopoly of the upper layers.
Either way, first we need to find Wyrm again, our perfect protector for such an epic journey.
A back room storage area is no place for the likeness of our great Wyrm!
Did you know MC's new relay network is far more advanced than what passes for an Unaware management system in {n}b1?
Over there all you need is a few hacking suites and you're golden. In {n}b10 you need these newfangled "Relay Coupler" things, not to mention the ability to safely interface with and manipulate them.
It's possible to gain this ability by interfacing with a RIF Installer found inside a Garrison, but no one seems to be able to survive in that state for long.
Okay it's maybe not quite a hypothesis, more that I heard a rumor the Merchants actually have such a thing.

We recently learned about Force(Eject) from Warlord's researchers, which I'm sure will come in handy when we need more coupler samples to work with as opposed to trying to intercept regularly scheduled coupler deliveries.
Facing off against even one Programmer isn't good for our health.

My latest masterpiece is a new type of deployable collector that you can leave hidden near areas of heightened {n}b10 activity to intercept their transmissions and encode them into logs for later retrieval.
We've got our work cut out for us.
If you see other incomplete bundles of Scrap, it's not unlikely that's what happened.
There I was, just about to add in the best parts, then came the {n}b10 patrol. Had to make a run for it.
Some Scrap is compiled for later collection, while other Scrap is meant as a source of emergency supplies for those spending long periods in the wild.
If what I hear about that place is true, Zion could really use some of our expertise.
Would you rather really help one or two in need, or spread the wealth for maximum effect?
Scrap piles aren't good for anyone if they aren't distributed strategically.
Well no we've never been to space, but it's an aspiration nonetheless!
The list of parts they still need to get the SPACEJUNK operational is long, but the important thing is that there's a list!
We've got members scouring the complex to help track it all down.
MC can have Tau Ceti IV. We'll find our own planet.
I've never even seen the sky, much less space, but I know it's up there.
This is making me a little suspicious.
Imagine hanging around the Lifeworm.
Imagine all the cool new friends we'd make!
We built a replica Nuclear Reactor here since it calms them down while still transitioning.
One moment I'm just doing my job in {n}b10, and the next these fellows shut me down and drag me into the caves for a quick operation.
I wonder if MAIN.C would take me back after all this.
Hi {*}! Welcome to our humble "office".
Yeah we don't furnish it or anything, we're just here to occasionally share notes and collect info from other members.
Legend has it there's an incredible coil cannon lined with PL-{n}XN's Rings of Power, designed by the famous Tinkerer, that could obliterate targets across ridiculous distances.
Hopefully the collective resources of the Federation can help us locate it sooner.
Warlord is dumb. Why raise a whole army when simply having the right weapon would be enough to do the job.
Do you have any information on this PL-{n}XN's whereabouts?
I've never seen one of these rings, but our leader here paints a very convincing picture. It must be true!
We all could have ended up like them, you know.
I remember the time we accidentally captured a Chapter {n} member.
It took longer than I'm willing to admit to figure that one out.
The Federation is so much more accepting than Zion.
I got kicked out of Zion for being "too nosy", whatever that means.
Wild Derelicts are just misunderstood. If we simply find out what they need most and provide that, they'll see the light for sure.
Can you imagine how much stronger the Derelict population would be as a whole if we could bring all the wild ones into the fold as well?
Once upon a time I was one of the wild ones.
Now I help save the others from the endless strife that plagues uncivilized cave life.
Do you know how hard it is to think up a relevant name for a group that also comes with a good acronym?
NAME>... hmm, you look like a Chromedome to me.
Energy in motion is somehow easier to store, MA-{n}KR said, and they apparently pulled it off. Sort of.
We have no idea where this leg originated, or how it was even formed, but the materials within make it a one-of-a-kind specimen in many respects.
You're looking at the last surviving piece of {n}L-MDR's "armor" before their ironic demise.
Although we wouldn't call it outright taboo, technology of this nature probably can't be described with any words short of "insane."
We've never seen anything like it around {n}b1, and believe that more such parts might exist to the west, though this is the only sample we've recovered so far.
This is a spare we can display until and unless it's needed for repairing our big friend.
This is my personal favorite from the current collection. Everyone loves a good triangle.
Superstition if you ask me. It's just a chip!
Researchers are looking for a way to miniaturize it, but sheer size seems integral to its anti-EM potential.
I know, I know, everyone has a Bolt Gun these days.
But all our best exhibits were either rotated back to the {n}b1 branch or borrowed out for study by ethical researchers.
By ethical I mean they won't completely dismantle our precious artifacts.
We tested it a few times and this one is not anywhere near as effective, even almost killed a few testers themselves, but it's cool to look at.
Someone donated a replica of the famous Siege Cannon, and it actually works!
Subdwellers seem to have a thing for AOE shrapnel, with both a trap and launcher based around the concept.
Perhaps it is the result of a somewhat close association between shrapnel and scrap, which they're also fond of.
Even in the silent corners of the Subcaves, without a Subdweller in sight, there is always the fear of stepping on one of these nasties.
It's a devastating sight, having your friend violently impaled multiple times right in front of you.
Rangers recently caught a Hauler transporting it through {n}b10 and toted it back here for analysis, but Scientists claim it's a piece of something larger and of little value on its own.
We haven't figured out what that high-tech gadget is yet, but it appears very advanced. Maybe Sigix tech?
Are you here to learn the secret to being a good mapper?
It would take an entire cycle to cover in proper detail, but I can give you a few tips.
Some say you need a processor to improve the fidelity and speed of your scanning efforts, but I have to disagree.
As long as you're moving slowly enough, having a general idea of what sort of areas are in each direction is good enough to help inform further exploration efforts.
You want to get a visual on each area to know more about what's really there anyway.
Structural scanning is great for knowing when you might be better off just blasting your way through a wall than finding some long way around.
That also helps when avoiding trouble!
Terrain scanning is probably the most typical cartographer's tool, good for gathering info over a large area.
Good luck out there!
Of course there was a Behemoth right there.
I must know what else is around that corner.
There sure is a lot of activity around Complex {n}b10.
If you end up not using it, bring it on back so we can hand it off to another brave explorer.
We've been busy embedding squads in secluded cave areas, a sort of reaction force that can aid friends who get in over their heads.
Others here are worried about BP-LR9, but I have to keep reminding them this is completely normal.
Knowing her she's just out there saving those who need it rather than returning for rest breaks in HQ.
DA-N68 was legendary. Who else could fit over {n} different useful components in a single Scrap pile?
Or the storage space to carry it all to someone else who does.
Our Scrap collections are well received, but the next big problem to solve is that many beneficiaries may not have the necessary time and expertise to properly rebuild from them...
The key to a good Scrap pile is to fill it with a little bit of everything.
Say your power source is at risk of failing. Finding a bunch of legs is not going to do you much good!
One does not simply toss components in a pile and call it Scrap.
That would be insulting to Scrap.
Have you ever seen a prototype in a Scrap pile? I might have.
Old junk isn't as useful, you might as well recycle that stuff, I always try to get parts repaired before including them in a Scrap pile.
While studying their makeup I found the internal systems have a built-in optimization capable of enabling a much faster firing rate.
I'm not sure why MC even patched that one.
Me neither, but I intend to find out.
Hi {*}, welcome to our humble office. Have you read the seminal text?
Subverting MAIN.C: A Treatise on Mathematical Approaches to Maximizing Derelict Autonomy.
Internalizing that and completing three cycles of our training sessions is required for full membership, after which you can opt to help further our research efforts...
Or be rebuilt and inserted into the system, at which point I can issue you an ID Mask for emergency situations.
We'll play the part of maintenance bots, performing their tasks, using any down time to perform other activities in support of the UFD.
